decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Growth in household spending has strengthened.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Since the beginning of the year, the housing sector has continued to improve and the drag from net exports appears to have lessened, but business fixed investment has been soft.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Since the beginning of the year, the housing sector has improved further but business fixed investment and net exports have been soft.”

changes.quote: Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and falling prices of n…”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recen…”

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting further improvement in labor market conditions and a return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.31% APR costs about $51.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.6% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.66% would fall by about $3.38 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.8%, and employers added an average of 165k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (May 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.19% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 97%, cut 0%, hike 2%.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
